solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Artist abused cannabis for creativity, primarily

indicators.note: something abused is misused and knocked out of shape, so these letters get rearranged
primarily points to the first thing, so only the opening letter of the word before it is used

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram material
taken as written, as anagram material
the opening letter of creativity

explanation.surface: A painter is accused of misusing marijuana to boost his creative output.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' does double duty in the surface but here it is part of the letters to rearrange, alongside cannabis and the first letter of creativity.
explanation.definitionFit: Francis Bacon was the twentieth-century Irish-born British painter known for his distorted figures, so he is an example of an artist.

clue.text: Comparatively dim footballers on Italian team

indicators.note: in a down clue, one piece sitting on another means it is placed above it, so it comes first

blocks.note: the Football Association, the body governing English football
Inter Milan, the Italian football club

explanation.surface: A disparaging remark about a dull group of players lining up for an Italian club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Comparatively dim' sounds like a jibe at the footballers' intelligence, but it is the definition, a comparative adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Fainter is the comparative form of faint, meaning less bright or less distinct, matching dimmer in degree.

clue.text: Instil spirit in a prisoner having returned home

indicators.note: something that has returned has gone back the way it came, so the word home is read right to left

blocks.note: taken as written
being in means being at home; it is the first part of inmate, the prisoner, and that part is turned round
an inmate is a prisoner; with its opening home part handled separately, the rest of the word remains

explanation.surface: Someone tries to lift the morale of a convict who has just come back home.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the home part of the prisoner word turns round; the rest of that word stays as it is.
explanation.definitionFit: To animate someone is to bring them to life or fill them with energy, the same as giving them spirit.

clue.text: Covered in geometric pattern, old- fashioned areas of shop

indicators.note: a thing covered in something else is wrapped by it, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: checks are a pattern of squares
something out is no longer in fashion

explanation.surface: A description of a dated shop interior decorated with chequered tiles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old-fashioned' gives OUT, as in 'that style is out'; 'Covered in' wraps it in the pattern word.
explanation.definitionFit: Checkouts are the tills in a supermarket where customers pay, the parts of a shop set aside for that.

clue.text: Several heard Pixar film review

indicators.note: heard means we go by how the word before it sounds when spoken, not by its spelling

blocks.note: some means several, and sounds like sum
Up is a 2009 Pixar animated film

explanation.surface: Several people listen to a critic's verdict on a Pixar movie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'review' looks like a film review, but it is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To sum up is to go over the main points briefly, which is what reviewing something at the end of a discussion does.

clue.text: Certain post is excellent support comprising metal, primarily

indicators.note: a thing comprising something else holds it within, so a letter is placed inside the support
primarily points to the first thing, so only the opening letter of the word before it is used

blocks.note: A1 means first-rate, written with the letters A and I
a rail is a bar that supports or holds something
the opening letter of metal

explanation.surface: A boast that some mail is superbly supported by a metal frame.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written AI in crosswords. The metal's letter goes just inside the support, after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Airmail is a particular kind of post, letters sent by aircraft, so it is a certain type of postal service.

clue.text: Soldiers in company crossing over river

indicators.note: a group crossing something straddles it on both sides, so a letter ends up inside the group's letters

blocks.note: OR stands for other ranks, soldiers who are not officers
taken as written
CO is the abbreviation for company
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over

explanation.surface: A military unit crossing a river on manoeuvres.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is not a container signal here; it simply supplies its own two letters. O for over comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: The Orinoco is one of the great rivers of South America, flowing through Venezuela.

clue.text: Basic requirements of head rub shown with arrows

blocks.note: nut is slang for the head
to sand is to rub a surface smooth
bolts are short heavy arrows fired from a crossbow

explanation.surface: A head massage offered alongside a display of archery arrows.
explanation.definitionFit: The nuts and bolts of something are its practical fundamentals, an idiom for the essential details.

clue.text: Employ universal surface covering going round indoors at edges

indicators.note: something going round another surrounds it, so the covering wraps the letters taken from indoors
the edges of a word are its two ends, so only its first and last letters are kept

blocks.note: U is the film classification for universal
a tile covers a floor, wall or roof
the outer letters of indoors

explanation.surface: Instructions to use one all-purpose covering on surfaces all round the edges inside a house.
explanation.walkthrough: U is the British film certificate meaning suitable for all, hence universal.
explanation.definitionFit: To utilise something is to put it to use, a more formal synonym of employ as a verb.

clue.text: Figure hit back against mass political ideology

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the two preceding words are read right to left

blocks.note: six is a figure, a number
to ram is to hit hard
M is the symbol for mass in physics

explanation.surface: A public figure lashes out against mass political doctrine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Figure' feels like a person, but it is a number; 'back' turns both of the first two words round together.
explanation.definitionFit: Marxism is the body of political and economic theory set out by Karl Marx, a classic example of a political doctrine.

clue.text: Force sides to unite and survive financially

blocks.note: to make someone do something is to force them
the ends of something are its sides or extremities
to meet is to come together

explanation.surface: A call to compel two opposing camps to come together.
explanation.definitionFit: To make ends meet is an idiom for earning just enough money to cover one's living costs.

clue.text: Check seeing body's head in casket moved

indicators.note: a word's head is its front end, so only its first letter is kept
letters that are moved are shifted into new positions, giving a fresh order

blocks.note: the opening letter of body
taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Someone checks the head of a corpse after the coffin has been shifted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check' looks like a verb about inspecting the body, but it is a noun meaning a halt to progress.
explanation.definitionFit: A setback is a reversal that halts progress, which is what a check (as in a check to one's plans) also means.

clue.text: Bird strike with beak catches raccoon regularly

indicators.note: something that catches another holds it inside, so letters are placed within the strike
regularly means at even intervals, so every other letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: to peck is to strike with the beak
the second, fourth and sixth letters of raccoon

explanation.surface: A bird pecks at a raccoon that has wandered too close.
explanation.definitionFit: The peacock is the male peafowl, a large bird famed for its fanned tail.

clue.text: Language used in minor's education

indicators.note: letters used in a phrase are contained within it, so the answer sits inside the words that follow

blocks.note: found across the words, starting in minor's and ending in education

explanation.surface: A note that a certain language features in a child's schooling.
explanation.definitionFit: Norse is the medieval Scandinavian tongue, a language of the Vikings.

clue.text: Poorly diminished by issue that's disagreeable

indicators.note: something diminished has been made smaller, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: poorly means ill or unwell
to issue is to come out or emerge

explanation.surface: A patient feels worse because of some unpleasant problem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Poorly' is British for ill, and 'issue' is a verb meaning emerge; 'by' simply places one piece next to the other.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unwelcome is not wanted or pleasing, which is what disagreeable describes.

clue.text: Swung a hip performing household task

indicators.note: a performer moves about, so the letters are set dancing into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Someone sways their hips while doing a chore around the house.
explanation.walkthrough: Washing-up is the British term for doing the dishes.
explanation.definitionFit: Washing-up, cleaning the dishes after a meal, is a standard chore in the home.

clue.text: Spooner's to manipulate supports for items of furniture

indicators.note: Spooner was famed for swapping the starting sounds of words, so the opening sounds of two words trade places

blocks.note: to cook figures is to manipulate them, and bases are supports; Spooner swaps their opening sounds

explanation.surface: A reference to Spooner's attempt to rig the legs holding up some furniture.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of COOK BASES gives BOOK CASES.
explanation.definitionFit: Bookcases are sets of shelves for holding books, standard pieces of household furniture.

clue.text: Ride across US city quietly

blocks.note: to go over something is to go across it
LA is Los Angeles
p, piano, is the musical direction to play quietly

explanation.surface: Someone drives quietly across an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ride' looks like a journey, but it is the verb used of things that slide up over one another, as clothes ride up.
explanation.definitionFit: When one thing rides over another it partly covers it, which is to overlap.

clue.text: Supplier of rocks and loam transported aboard vessel

indicators.note: something transported is carried off elsewhere, so the letters are moved into a new order
cargo carried aboard a vessel sits inside it, so letters go within the vessel's word

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram material
a can is a container, a vessel

explanation.surface: A cargo of stone and soil is being shipped by boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rocks' here means lumps of coal; a coalman delivered coal door to door in sacks.
explanation.definitionFit: A coalman sells and delivers coal, which comes in hard lumps, so he supplies rocks in a playful sense.

clue.text: Put forward initial tips to soft-boil egg in shell

indicators.note: initial tips are the front ends of words, so only first letters are kept
in places the selected letters inside the shell that follows

blocks.note: a pod is the shell of a pea or bean
the first letters of soft-boil and egg

explanation.surface: Someone offers first tips on how to soft-boil an egg in its shell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'egg in shell' tempts you to put O inside something, but egg only lends its first letter; the shell is the pea pod.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose a question or idea is to put it forward for consideration.

clue.text: Potential danger behind going upside- down within capsule, perhaps

indicators.note: in a down clue, turning upside down sends the word upwards, so it reads backwards
within places the overturned word inside the capsule

blocks.note: aft means towards the rear of a ship
a capsule is one kind of pill; perhaps marks it as an example

explanation.surface: A warning about a capsule tumbling inside some vehicle or pod.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, upside-down means read from the bottom up. 'perhaps' flags the capsule as just one kind of pill.
explanation.definitionFit: A pitfall is a hidden hazard or trap, a risk that may catch someone out.

clue.text: Persist going around bars

indicators.note: letters going around circulate and land in new places, so their order is mixed up

blocks.note: taken as written, as anagram material

explanation.surface: Someone keeps doing the rounds of the local pubs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' suggests pubs, but it means bands of colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Stripes are long narrow bands, and bars is a synonym for such bands of colour or marking.

clue.text: Direction for sailor: haul fish back

indicators.note: going back means travelling the opposite way, so the two preceding words are read right to left

blocks.note: to draw is to pull or haul
an eel is a fish

explanation.surface: A sailor is told which way to pull in the catch.
explanation.definitionFit: Leeward is the side or direction away from the wind, a nautical bearing used at sea.

clue.text: No idea of pair of names appearing in double act

indicators.note: appearing in something means being inside it, so the letters go within the double act

blocks.note: a duo is a pair of performers
N is short for name, and a pair gives two of them

explanation.surface: A comedy pair who can't remember each other's names.
explanation.walkthrough: N for name is a standard dictionary abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dunno is a casual spelling of 'don't know', the reply of someone with no idea.

clue.text: Sample from painter impressed caretaker

indicators.note: a sample is a piece taken from a larger whole, so the answer is lifted out of the words that follow

blocks.note: found across the words, starting in painter and ending in impressed

explanation.surface: A building's caretaker is struck by a sample of an artist's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caretaker' is an adjective here, as in a caretaker government, not the person who looks after a building.
explanation.definitionFit: A caretaker manager or government serves temporarily until a permanent one is chosen, just as an interim one does.

clue.text: Ancient monarch's single brother spurning king

indicators.note: to spurn is to reject, so the letter for king is thrown out

blocks.note: solo means alone, single
a monk is a brother in a religious order
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king

explanation.surface: An ancient king's unmarried brother refuses to accept the throne.
explanation.walkthrough: MONK loses K to give MON. The definition carries the clue's 's (Solomon is) and the setter treats it as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Solomon was the biblical king of Israel, son of David, famed for his wisdom, so an ancient ruler.

clue.text: Clutch fruit, squeezing peel, extracting innards

indicators.note: removing the innards takes out the middle, so only the outer letters stay
something squeezing another holds it tightly inside, so letters are pressed into the fruit

blocks.note: a grape is a fruit
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone grips a piece of fruit, squeezing it until the inside pops out of the skin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'peel' is used as a word to be gutted, not as the fruit's skin.
explanation.definitionFit: To grapple is to seize and grip firmly, and to clutch is likewise to grasp tightly.

clue.text: They gauge views on poison spill at sea

indicators.note: being at sea means being confused and adrift, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters of the printed words, less the one surplus S that the setter's slip left in

explanation.surface: Pollsters canvass public opinion about a toxic spill in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed fodder has one S too many: 'on poison pill' would give the answer exactly, so the extra S is a slip in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinion polls are surveys that measure public attitudes, so they gauge people's views.
